candidate.title: Align codebook residual displacement with directed behavior residuals
candidate.equation: For x in {source,target}, define p_xc = softmax_c(-||x-c||^2/tau) and mu_x = sum_c p_xc c. Let r_x = x - mu_x and v = r_target - r_source. Let g = sigmoid((||target||^2-||source||^2)/scale). L = weight * mean_mask[g * (||v||^2 - 2 * dot(v, target-source))].

symbols.source: Source item representation for each behavior pair.
symbols.target: Target item representation for each behavior pair.
symbols.codebook: Shared codebook vectors c indexed by c.
symbols.p_xc: Soft assignment probability of representation x to codeword c.
symbols.r_x: Residual from the soft codebook representative to representation x.
symbols.v: Directed change in residual from source to target.
symbols.g: Asymmetric pair weight derived from the target-source difference in squared representation norms.
symbols.scale: Scale for the asymmetric pair weight.
symbols.weight: Composition weight for this auxiliary loss.
symbols.mask: Validity mask; only valid pairs contribute to the mean.

candidate.behaviour_signal: The directed change in the source and target residuals after their soft codebook representatives are removed.
candidate.codebook_interaction: The codebook gradient changes both residual estimates through the source and target soft representatives, and it aligns their directed residual displacement v with the observed target-source displacement. It does not minimize the distance between the two endpoint codewords or pull them toward a common representative. The asymmetric weight and directed dot product make the loss change when endpoints are exchanged.
candidate.encoder_interaction: The loss has gradients with respect to both representations, but the host discards encoder-only gradients. Its intended effect on exported codes comes from its nonzero codebook gradient.
candidate.risk: Residual displacement may be dominated by representation scale or noise rather than behaviorally useful structure. Since the loss uses soft representatives, it may improve residual alignment while changing hard assignments in a way that increases code concentration or reduces prefix diversity.
candidate.falsifier: Reject if the probe finds a zero or non-finite codebook gradient or no loss change after exchanging source and target. Falsify the mechanism after training if pair-codeword separation shrinks materially, any required usage, prefix, drift, or information threshold is breached, or Stage-3 recall@10 fails to exceed the archived control.
candidate.why_not_the_measured_failures: Unlike the inert encoder-only candidates, this term has a direct soft-representative path to the codebook. Unlike the collapsed pairwise cross-entropy, it aligns the directed residual change to the observed behavior displacement rather than assigning both endpoints to the same code. It is a residual-geometry objective, distinct from direct codeword-margin geometry and assignment-usage regularization.
